chains.title: AR-bound distal enhancer regulates RFX6

links.claim: AR is proposed to bind the ref T allele more strongly than the alt C allele. This relies on the literature quote reporting allele-specific AR chromatin occupancy with the T allele enhancing AR binding (E09d), not on a supplied AR QBiC-SELEX model; no AR QBiC-SELEX model is supplied, and E10 shows no AR ChIP-seq peak over this exact variant in LNCaP, so the binding evidence is weak.
The variant lies inside EH38E2496909, a distal enhancer-like cCRE (dELS), consistent with an active regulatory element; the ENCODE z-scores are maxima across biosamples, not LNCaP-specific.

RFX6 is the nearest gene and the strongest L2G target at the locus (E02, E07, E09c), but no RFX6 prostate eQTL is shown and E11 reports no significant prostate eQTL for this variant; an element-to-RFX6 regulatory link is therefore plausible but unproven.

The relevant context is AR-positive prostate cancer/tumor cells; E09d supports AR-driven chromatin in prostate tumors, but the supplied LNCaP ENCODE data show no TF ChIP peak containing this variant (E04), including no AR peak (E10), so LNCaP-specific occupancy is not demonstrated.

The locus is associated with prostate cancer (E06) and RFX6 is supported by L2G and literature as a candidate target (E07, E09a-c), but a causal AR-dependent RFX6 mechanism is not directly demonstrated; allele direction is contested because E09d calls T the risk/AR-enhancing allele while E06 reports C as the prostate cancer effect allele.

predictions: Allele-specific AR occupancy at this element is higher on the ref T allele than the alt C allele in AR-positive prostate cancer cells/tumors.
RFX6 expression or an RFX6-dependent phenotype tracks the AR-high T allele/AR activity in prostate cancer models; the direction may be activation or repression.
The dELS contacts RFX6 and perturbation of the element alters RFX6 expression.
falsified_if: No allele-specific AR occupancy is observed at this base in AR-positive prostate cancer cells or tumors.
No RFX6 eQTL, chromatin contact, or perturbation effect links this dELS to RFX6.
The prostate cancer association is fully explained by a linked variant with no AR effect at this base.

predictions: No allele-specific AR occupancy at this base in AR-positive prostate cancer cells or tumors.
No RFX6 or GPRC6A prostate eQTL or allele-dependent regulatory effect attributable to this base.

The association is driven by a linked causal variant or another element.
falsified_if: Allele-specific AR occupancy at this base and an RFX6 or GPRC6A regulatory effect are demonstrated in prostate cancer cells or tumors.

Dysregulated expression or mutations of the RFX6 gene in prostate cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma, gastric cancer, melanoma, and other tumors have garnered significant interest, with studies showing that such alterations affect tumor cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, and are correlated with an unfavorable clinical prognosis in patients carrying RFX6 mutations.
Furthermore, examination of RFX6 target genes reveals a potential association with tumor development, indicating that RFX6 may play a role in cancer progression.

Here the FinnGen cohort phenome-wide analysis, along with multiple genome-wide association studies, has consistently identified the rs[masked]-RFX6/6q22 locus associated with prostate cancer (PCa) risk across diverse populations.
It is uncovered that rs[masked] resides in a reprogrammed androgen receptor (AR) binding site in PCa tumors, with the T risk allele enhancing AR chromatin occupancy.
